exposure: Experiences in the first perinatal period (e.g., prenatal attitude towards vaginal birth, perceived maternal-infant bonding, post-traumatic stress symptoms)
outcome: Preference for vaginal birth in a future birth
cohort: 394 individuals with a first cesarean birth and a second birth during the 5-year follow-up period from the First Baby Study
finding: Individuals who preferred vaginal birth in a future birth had nearly 8 times higher odds of attempting a vaginal birth after cesarean (LAC).
mod_finding: Preference for vaginal birth was strongly associated with attempting a vaginal birth after cesarean (LAC).
